done_when: Close starts the review at the same time as its tests, so a round takes about as long as the slower of the two; a red test or a P0/P1 finding still stops the round, and both results are reported together. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body: Raise: Functional. When a previously ready, non-draft pull request gets a new commit whose local tests fail, close pushes that commit and publishes a clean review before refusing at this line. `_publish` only makes an existing pull request draft for a blocked review (`src/forge/close.py:650–667`), and `forge-pr-check` checks the review but not the saved test failure (`src/forge/prcheck.py:237–249`). In a supported repo whose required checks omit `tests`, the pull request can therefore be merged despite the red test. The same exposure occurs where draft pull requests are unsupported.
findings.title: A red local test can leave an existing pull request mergeable

findings.body: Raise: Functional. Close now prints only `tested` here, removing its separate print of every `No local test names` warning. The pytest picker emits one warning per uncovered changed source file (`src/forge/fasttest.py:313–315`), but `review.test_run` caps its returned report at the first 50 and last 30 selected lines (`src/forge/review.py:368–375`). In a realistic bulk change of 100 source modules without named tests, warnings in the middle disappear from close's output, so workers cannot see every file whose local test coverage was missed.
findings.title: Close drops source-file test warnings from large changes
